q23525.en: Overtaking is allowed in poor visibility, as long as you flash your lights during the manoeuvre.

explain.short: With poor visibility you cannot see oncoming traffic. Flashing your lights does not make overtaking safe or legal.
explain.rule: Overtaking is forbidden near bends, crests and whenever visibility is poor (fog, heavy rain).
explain.trap: 'purché' (as long as) adds a condition that sounds safe but does not make the overtake legal.

sceneParams.caption: Fog: no overtaking, flashing lights don't help

q23526.en: Overtaking on a bend is forbidden even if the road has two separate carriageways.

explain.short: On a road with two separate carriageways no traffic comes towards you, so overtaking on a bend is allowed.
explain.rule: On bends and crests you may overtake only if the road has separate carriageways or at least two marked lanes in your direction.
explain.trap: 'anche se' (even if) makes the ban sound total, but separate carriageways are exactly the exception.

sceneParams.caption: Separate carriageways: bend overtaking is allowed

q23527.en: Overtaking on a bend is forbidden even if the road has at least two lanes in each direction.

explain.short: With two or more marked lanes in your direction, you stay in your own half of the road, so overtaking on a bend is allowed.
explain.rule: On bends and crests you may overtake if there are at least two marked lanes for your direction of travel.
explain.trap: 'anche se' (even if) hides the exception: two lanes per direction make it allowed.

sceneParams.caption: Two lanes your way: bend overtaking is allowed

keywords.it: due corsie per senso di marcia

q23528.en: Overtaking vehicles that are stopped at a level crossing without barriers is allowed if the train is far away.

explain.short: Near a level crossing without barriers overtaking is forbidden. The distance of the train does not change this.
explain.rule: No overtaking at or near level crossings without barriers (unless traffic lights control the crossing).
explain.trap: 'se il treno è distante' (if the train is far away) is a false excuse: the ban does not depend on the train.

sceneParams.caption: Level crossing without barriers: no overtaking

q23529.en: Overtaking slow-moving vehicles at a level crossing without barriers is allowed if the train is far away.

explain.short: The ban on overtaking near level crossings without barriers applies always, also to slow vehicles.
explain.rule: No overtaking at or near level crossings without barriers (unless traffic lights control the crossing).
explain.trap: 'in lento movimento' (moving slowly) and 'treno distante' (train far away) do not create an exception.

sceneParams.caption: Slow cars at a level crossing: still no overtaking

q23530.en: Overtaking at junctions is allowed as long as nobody is coming from the right.

explain.short: At a junction a car can appear or turn at any moment. Overtaking there is forbidden, except in specific cases (lights, a traffic officer, a priority road with lanes).
explain.rule: As a rule, no overtaking at or near intersections (incroci).
explain.trap: 'purché' (as long as) offers a condition that is not one of the legal exceptions.

sceneParams.caption: Junction without lights: no overtaking

q23531.en: Overtaking in acceleration lanes is allowed as long as it is done carefully.

explain.short: The acceleration lane is only for speeding up to join the main road. You must not use it to overtake.
explain.rule: Acceleration and deceleration lanes are not for overtaking.
explain.trap: 'con attenzione' (carefully) does not make a forbidden manoeuvre legal.

sceneParams.caption: Acceleration lane: only to join, not to overtake

q23532.en: It is always allowed to pass a two-wheeled vehicle.

explain.short: Bicycles and motorbikes are vehicles too. All the normal overtaking bans (bends, crests, solid lines, poor visibility) still apply.
explain.rule: Pass a two-wheeled vehicle only where overtaking is allowed, with enough side distance.
explain.trap: 'sempre' (always) is a trap word: almost nothing in the highway code is 'always' allowed.

lines: Bends, crests, solid lines: no overtaking
sceneParams.caption: Bikes too: normal overtaking bans apply

q23533.en: Overtaking is forbidden on one-way roads.

explain.short: On a one-way road nobody comes towards you, so overtaking is allowed (on the left, when safe).
explain.rule: On one-way roads you may overtake, even near bends and crests, if the normal safety checks are OK.
explain.trap: The word 'vietato' (forbidden) is wrong here: one-way roads make overtaking easier, not forbidden.

sceneParams.caption: One-way road: overtaking is allowed

explain.short: A police car that is not on an emergency call is a normal vehicle for overtaking. You may pass it where overtaking is allowed.
explain.rule: You must not get in the way of police on an emergency call (blue lights and siren). Otherwise normal rules apply.
explain.trap: There is no general ban on passing 'veicoli della polizia' (police vehicles); only emergency service matters.

sceneParams.caption: Police not on emergency: you may overtake

q23535.en: On the motorway you can overtake on the right or on the left, as you like.

explain.short: Overtaking is done on the left, also on the motorway. Overtaking on the right is allowed only in a few special cases.
explain.rule: Always overtake on the left. On the motorway, overtaking on the right is normally forbidden.
explain.trap: 'indifferentemente' (either way / as you like) is the trap: right and left are not the same.

sceneParams.caption: Motorway: no overtaking on the right

q23536.en: Motorbikes can overtake each other on both the right and the left.

explain.short: Motorbikes follow the same rule as cars: overtake on the left. Passing on the right is not allowed just because there is room.
explain.rule: Overtaking is on the left. Right-side overtaking only in the special cases of the code (e.g. a car turning left).
explain.trap: 'sia a destra che a sinistra' (both right and left) is false: motorbikes have no special right-side privilege.

sceneParams.caption: Motorbikes: overtake on the left, not the right

keywords.it: sia a destra che a sinistra
keywords.en: both on the right and the left

q23537.en: The space needed to overtake increases if the vehicle being overtaken slows down.

explain.short: If the other vehicle slows down, you pass it faster. So you need less space, not more.
explain.rule: The bigger the speed difference, the shorter the overtake. A vehicle that speeds up makes it longer.
explain.trap: 'aumenta' (increases) is the trap: when the other car 'rallenta' (slows down), the space gets smaller.

sceneParams.caption: Other car slows: overtake needs LESS space

q23538.en: The space needed to overtake does not depend on the length of the vehicles.

explain.short: A long truck, or your car with a caravan, takes longer to pass. So the space needed is bigger.
explain.rule: Overtaking space depends on speeds and on the length of both vehicles.
explain.trap: 'indipendente' (independent / does not depend) is wrong: length matters a lot.

sceneParams.caption: Long truck: the overtake needs more space

q23539.en: It is forbidden to overtake a bus that is stopped to let passengers get on and off.

explain.short: You may pass a stopped bus, if the road is clear. Go slowly and watch for people crossing in front of it.
explain.rule: Passing a bus stopped at a bus stop is allowed, with care for pedestrians.
explain.trap: 'vietato' (forbidden) is wrong: the rule asks for care, not a ban.

sceneParams.caption: Bus at a stop: pass slowly, watch for people

q23540.en: Overtaking is forbidden on bends and crests of one-way roads.

explain.short: On a one-way road there is no oncoming traffic, so overtaking on bends and crests is allowed.
explain.rule: The bend/crest ban protects you from oncoming cars. On one-way roads it does not apply.
explain.trap: Do not mix up 'curve e dossi' (bends and crests) with 'senso unico' (one-way): one-way is the exception.

sceneParams.caption: One-way road: bend overtaking is allowed

q23541.en: Overtaking is forbidden if you have to cross the dashed longitudinal line.

explain.short: A dashed line can be crossed. That is exactly the line that lets you overtake.
explain.rule: Dashed line: you may cross it to overtake. Solid line: you must not cross it.
explain.trap: 'tratteggiata' (dashed) is not 'continua' (solid). Only the solid line forbids crossing.

sceneParams.caption: Dashed line: you may cross it to overtake

q23542.en: Overtaking motorcycles on the right is allowed if there is enough space.

explain.short: Enough space is not a reason to pass on the right. Motorcycles are overtaken on the left like other vehicles.
explain.rule: Overtake on the left. Right-side overtaking only in the special cases listed by the code.
explain.trap: 'se vi è spazio sufficiente' (if there is enough space) sounds reasonable but is not a legal exception.

sceneParams.caption: Motorbike ahead: never pass on the right

q23543.en: In heavy traffic, motorcyclists may use the reserved lanes to overtake.

explain.short: Reserved lanes are only for the vehicles shown on the signs (for example buses and taxis). Heavy traffic does not change this.
explain.rule: Do not drive or overtake in a reserved lane unless your vehicle is allowed in it.
explain.trap: 'intenso traffico' (heavy traffic) is a false excuse; 'corsie riservate' means reserved lanes.

sceneParams.caption: Reserved lanes: not for overtaking

q23544.en: When you start overtaking, you are allowed to signal the manoeuvre to the vehicles ahead by flashing your high-beam headlights.

explain.short: A short flash of the headlights is a legal way to warn the driver ahead that you are about to pass. Do it briefly, so you do not dazzle anyone.
explain.rule: You may warn the vehicle ahead with a brief headlight flash (or the horn outside towns). The left indicator is always required.
explain.trap: 'è consentito' (it is allowed) means you may do it, not that you must.

sceneParams.caption: A brief headlight flash may warn the car ahead

q23545.en: When overtaking, you must adjust your speed to the speed of the vehicle you are overtaking.

explain.short: You need enough extra speed to pass quickly, but not too much. Your speed depends on how fast the other vehicle goes.
explain.rule: Pass with a clear but safe speed difference, always within the speed limit.
explain.trap: 'regolare la velocità' means adjust (adapt) your speed, not simply go as fast as possible.

sceneParams.caption: Adapt your speed to the car you pass

q23546.en: To overtake in towns, you may exceed the speed limit for a moment.

explain.short: Speed limits apply all the time, also during an overtake. If you cannot pass within the limit, do not overtake.
explain.rule: No exceeding the speed limit, not even briefly to overtake.
explain.trap: 'momentaneamente' (for a moment) is a trap: a short time does not make speeding legal.

lines: Can't pass within the limit? Don't
sceneParams.caption: Speed limits apply during overtaking too

q23547.en: When overtaking, you must keep strictly to the right.

explain.short: To overtake you move to the left, past the other vehicle. Keeping strictly right is what the overtaken driver does.
explain.rule: Overtake on the left, leaving enough side distance, then move back right.
explain.trap: The duty to 'mantenere strettamente la destra' (keep strictly right) belongs to the vehicle being overtaken.

sceneParams.caption: Move LEFT to overtake, with a side gap

q23548.en: When overtaking, you must not accelerate.

explain.short: The overtaking driver usually needs to speed up to pass quickly. Not accelerating is the duty of the driver being overtaken.
explain.rule: Overtaker: pass briskly, within the speed limit. Overtaken driver: do not speed up.
explain.trap: 'non bisogna accelerare' (you must not accelerate) is the rule for the other driver, not for you.

sceneParams.caption: The overtaker may speed up, within the limit

q23549.en: After overtaking you must move back right immediately, while slowing down.

explain.short: You return to the right only when you can do it safely, without cutting in. Slowing down in front of the other car is dangerous.
explain.rule: Move back right as soon as you can do it safely, leaving room for the overtaken vehicle.
explain.trap: 'immediatamente' (immediately) and 'rallentando' (slowing down) together describe a dangerous cut-in.

sceneParams.caption: Don't cut in and brake: return when safe

q23550.en: Overtaking public scheduled buses is forbidden.

explain.short: A public bus is a normal vehicle for overtaking. You may pass it where overtaking is allowed.
explain.rule: No special ban on overtaking buses. If a bus is stopped, pass carefully and watch for pedestrians.
explain.trap: 'autobus in servizio pubblico di linea' (public route bus) does not create a ban.

sceneParams.caption: Public bus: you may overtake it

q23551.en: Overtaking is forbidden when the vehicle ahead has switched on its right indicator.

explain.short: A car signalling right is going to turn right or pull over, leaving the road free on the left. You may overtake it, carefully.
explain.rule: It is a LEFT indicator that matters: you must not overtake on the left a car that signals a left turn.
explain.trap: Do not mix up 'destro' (right) and 'sinistro' (left).

sceneParams.caption: Car ahead signals right: you may pass left

q23552.en: Overtaking is forbidden if it is snowing.

explain.short: There is no specific ban for snow. But snow reduces grip and visibility, so overtake only if it is really safe.
explain.rule: Overtaking is forbidden when visibility is poor; snow alone is not a ban, but needs extra care.
explain.trap: Do not invent bans: 'se nevica' (if it snows) is not in the list of forbidden places or cases.

sceneParams.caption: Snow: no automatic ban, but extra care

explain.short: A passo carrabile (a driveway entrance) is a place where you must not park. It does not ban overtaking.
explain.rule: Driveways forbid stopping and parking, not overtaking.
explain.trap: 'passi carrabili' (driveways) are about parking, not overtaking: don't mix the two topics.

lines: No parking in front of it
sceneParams.caption: Driveway: no parking, but overtaking is OK

explain.short: There is no rule that bans overtaking near hospitals. Near a hospital you should avoid noise, for example the horn.
explain.rule: Near hospitals: drive calmly and avoid using the horn. Overtaking follows the normal rules.
explain.trap: 'in prossimità degli ospedali' (near hospitals) is not on the list of places where overtaking is banned.

sceneParams.caption: Near a hospital: no overtaking ban

q23555.en: Overtaking is forbidden near service stations.

explain.short: Service (fuel) stations are not on the list of places where overtaking is banned. Just watch for cars entering and leaving.
explain.rule: Overtaking near a service station follows the normal rules.
explain.trap: 'stazioni di servizio' (service stations) is a made-up ban.

lines: Watch cars going in and out
sceneParams.caption: Near a fuel station: no overtaking ban

q23556.en: Overtaking near a crest is allowed on one-way roads.

explain.short: On a one-way road nobody comes towards you from behind the crest, so overtaking is allowed there.
explain.rule: On crests and bends you may overtake on one-way roads, separate carriageways or roads with 2+ marked lanes your way.
explain.trap: 'dosso' (the top of a rise in the road) is normally a ban, but 'senso unico' (one-way) is an exception.

sceneParams.caption: One-way road: overtaking at a crest is allowed

q23557.en: Overtaking near a crest is allowed on one-way carriageways.

explain.short: On a one-way carriageway all traffic goes your way, so there is no risk of a head-on crash behind the crest.
explain.rule: On crests and bends you may overtake on one-way carriageways.
explain.trap: 'carreggiate a senso unico' (one-way carriageways) is the exception to the crest ban.

sceneParams.caption: One-way carriageway: crest overtaking is allowed

q23558.en: Overtaking near a crest is allowed on roads with two lanes in each direction.

explain.short: With two marked lanes for your direction, you overtake without entering the oncoming half of the road.
explain.rule: On crests and bends you may overtake if there are at least two marked lanes for your direction.
explain.trap: 'due corsie per senso di marcia' (two lanes per direction) is not the same as a two-lane road with one lane each way.

sceneParams.caption: Two lanes your way: crest overtaking is allowed

keywords.it: due corsie per senso di marcia

q23559.en: Overtaking near a crest is allowed on roads with two separate carriageways.

explain.short: Separate carriageways mean the oncoming traffic is on another road. Overtaking near a crest is allowed.
explain.rule: On crests and bends you may overtake on roads with separate carriageways.
explain.trap: 'carreggiate separate' (separate carriageways) is one of the exceptions to the crest ban.

sceneParams.caption: Separate carriageways: crest overtaking is allowed

q23560.en: It is forbidden to overtake by following closely behind an ambulance on an emergency call.

explain.short: You must not follow an emergency vehicle closely to use the free road it opens. Overtaking that way is forbidden and dangerous.
explain.rule: Give way to emergency vehicles with blue lights and siren; never follow them closely to get through traffic.
explain.trap: 'accodandosi' means getting right behind (queuing up behind) the ambulance.

sceneParams.caption: Never follow an ambulance to overtake

q23562.en: On two-lane two-way carriageways, near a crest, overtaking animal-drawn vehicles is allowed.

explain.short: On a road with one lane each way you cannot see oncoming traffic behind a crest. The ban applies to every vehicle, also slow carts.
explain.rule: Near crests on two-way roads with one lane each way: no overtaking.
explain.trap: 'veicoli a trazione animale' (animal-drawn vehicles) are slow, but slowness is not an exception.

sceneParams.caption: Crest on a two-way road: no overtaking

q23563.en: On two-lane two-way carriageways, near a crest, it is allowed to overtake by following in the slipstream of the vehicle ahead.

explain.short: Near a crest on a two-way road overtaking is forbidden. Following another overtaking car closely is even more dangerous, because you see nothing.
explain.rule: Near crests on two-way roads with one lane each way: no overtaking.
explain.trap: 'nella scia' (in the slipstream, right behind) does not give you the other car's right to pass.

sceneParams.caption: Crest: no overtaking, not even behind another car

q23564.en: Near a crest, you may drive into the opposite half of the road to overtake scheduled buses that are stopped for passengers.

explain.short: Behind a crest you cannot see oncoming cars. Moving into the opposite half there is forbidden, even to pass a stopped bus.
explain.rule: Near a crest on a two-way road, do not move into the opposite half of the road. Wait behind the bus.
explain.trap: 'invadere l'opposta semicarreggiata' means going into the oncoming half of the road: the dangerous part.

sceneParams.caption: Bus stopped near a crest: wait, don't pass

q23565.en: You cannot overtake at crests on a one-way carriageway with two lanes.

explain.short: On a one-way carriageway there is no oncoming traffic, so overtaking at a crest is allowed.
explain.rule: On crests and bends you may overtake on one-way carriageways.
explain.trap: 'non si può' (you cannot) is the trap: 'senso unico' (one-way) makes it allowed.

sceneParams.caption: One-way, two lanes: crest overtaking is allowed

q23566.en: You cannot overtake a vehicle that has signalled it wants to pull over to the right edge of the road.

explain.short: A car that pulls over to the right leaves the road free. You may pass it on the left, carefully.
explain.rule: You may overtake a vehicle that signals right or is pulling over, if the overtake is otherwise allowed.
explain.trap: 'accostarsi al margine destro' means pulling over to the right edge, which makes your overtake easier.

sceneParams.caption: Car pulling over right: you may pass left

q23567.en: You cannot overtake at the exit of a public car park.

explain.short: A car park exit is not a place where overtaking is banned. Just watch for cars coming out.
explain.rule: Overtaking near a car park exit follows the normal rules.
explain.trap: 'uscita di un pubblico parcheggio' (exit of a public car park) is not a legal ban.

sceneParams.caption: Car park exit: no overtaking ban

q23568.en: Overtaking is forbidden if on the left of the vehicle there is a broken white line next to a solid one.

explain.short: When the dashed line is on your side, you may cross it to overtake. The solid line only stops traffic from the other side.
explain.rule: Mixed lines: you may cross if the dashed line is next to you, not if the solid line is next to you.
explain.trap: Look which line is 'alla sinistra del veicolo' (on your left): here it is the 'discontinua' (dashed) one.

sceneParams.caption: Dashed line on your side: you may overtake

q23569.en: You cannot overtake on the right a tram that is running in the middle of the road.

explain.short: A tram running in the centre of the road is passed on the right, if there is enough room. This is one of the legal cases of overtaking on the right.
explain.rule: Trams moving in the middle of the road are overtaken on the right.
explain.trap: 'non si può' (you cannot) is wrong: trams in the centre are the classic exception.

sceneParams.caption: Tram in the middle: pass it on the right

keywords.en: in the middle of the road

q23570.en: While overtaking, the driver must avoid squeezing or cutting in on the vehicle being overtaken.

explain.short: If you cut in, the overtaken car must brake or swerve. You must return right only with enough space.
explain.rule: Return to the right gradually and safely, without cutting in on the overtaken vehicle.
explain.trap: 'tagliare la strada' means to cut in front of someone; 'stringere' means squeezing them.

sceneParams.caption: Cutting in forces the other car to brake

q23571.en: The danger of overtaking comes from the risk of hitting other vehicles that show they want to do the same manoeuvre.

explain.short: A car behind you may already be overtaking, or a car ahead may move out to overtake. That is why you check mirrors first.
explain.rule: Before overtaking, make sure no one behind has started to overtake you and no one ahead is moving out.
explain.trap: 'la stessa manovra' (the same manoeuvre) means other cars also overtaking.

sceneParams.caption: Check nobody else is overtaking first

q23572.en: The danger of overtaking comes from the risk of colliding with the vehicle to be overtaken while you approach it.

explain.short: If you get too close before starting, you can hit the vehicle ahead if it brakes. Keep a safe distance.
explain.rule: Keep a safe distance behind until you start the overtake.
explain.trap: 'in fase di avvicinamento' means while approaching (before passing).

sceneParams.caption: Keep your distance before you pull out

q23573.en: The danger of overtaking comes from the risk of colliding with the overtaken vehicle when you move back into your lane.

explain.short: If you return right too early, you can hit the car you just passed. Check it in your mirror first.
explain.rule: Move back right only when you see the overtaken vehicle in your mirror at a safe distance.
explain.trap: 'in fase di rientro' means while moving back into your lane.

sceneParams.caption: Returning too early can hit the car you passed

q23574.en: The danger of overtaking comes from the risk of a head-on crash with a vehicle coming from the opposite direction.

explain.short: On a two-way road you overtake in the half of the road used by oncoming traffic. A head-on crash is the worst risk.
explain.rule: Overtake only if the road ahead is clear for long enough.
explain.trap: 'urto frontale' means head-on crash; 'senso contrario' means opposite direction.

sceneParams.caption: Oncoming car: no overtaking

q23575.en: The danger of overtaking comes from the reduced width of the carriageway.

explain.short: On a narrow road there is little room beside the other vehicle and for oncoming traffic, so overtaking is more dangerous.
explain.rule: Overtake only where the road is wide enough to leave a safe side distance.
explain.trap: 'ridotta larghezza' means narrow width.

sceneParams.caption: Narrow road: overtaking is risky

q23576.en: While overtaking, the driver must stay in the overtaking lane for as long as possible.

explain.short: You should leave the overtaking lane as soon as you can do it safely. Staying there blocks faster traffic.
explain.rule: After passing, return right as soon as it is safe.
explain.trap: 'il più a lungo possibile' (as long as possible) is the opposite of the rule.

sceneParams.caption: Don't stay in the left lane: return when safe

q23577.en: While overtaking, the driver must keep signalling the manoeuvre with the horn the whole time.

explain.short: The horn is not required, and using it continuously is forbidden. You signal the overtake with the indicator.
explain.rule: Use the indicator. The horn only briefly, outside towns, and only if needed.
explain.trap: 'continuamente' (continuously) and 'è tenuto' (must) make this doubly wrong.

sceneParams.caption: No need to honk: use the indicator

q23578.en: While overtaking, the driver must keep a speed at least double that of the overtaken vehicle.

explain.short: There is no 'double speed' rule. You need a clear speed difference, but always within the speed limit.
explain.rule: Adapt your speed to the other vehicle and to the speed limit.
explain.trap: 'almeno doppia' (at least double) is an invented number.

sceneParams.caption: No 'double speed' rule; stay within the limit

q23579.en: The danger of overtaking comes from the presence of normal edge delineators on the road.

explain.short: Delineators (the posts at the road edge) help you see the road. They do not make overtaking dangerous.
explain.rule: Edge delineators are guides, especially at night; they are not a hazard.
explain.trap: 'delineatori normali di margine' are the white edge posts with reflectors.

lines: They show where the road goes
sceneParams.caption: Edge posts guide you, they're not a danger

q23580.en: Overtaking is forbidden at night in towns with poor street lighting.

explain.short: There is no such ban. At night you must check visibility and use the right lights, but overtaking is not automatically forbidden.
explain.rule: Overtaking is forbidden when you cannot see well ahead, not simply because it is night.
explain.trap: 'di notte' (at night) is not the same as 'scarsa visibilità' (poor visibility).

sceneParams.caption: Night in town: no automatic overtaking ban

q23581.en: Overtaking is forbidden when a dashed centre line is painted on the carriageway.

explain.short: A dashed centre line can be crossed. It is the line that allows overtaking.
explain.rule: Dashed centre line: overtaking allowed if safe. Solid centre line: no crossing.
explain.trap: 'tratteggiata' (dashed) is not 'continua' (solid).

sceneParams.caption: Dashed centre line: you may overtake

q23582.en: Overtaking is forbidden on mountain roads when you are behind a public bus.

explain.short: There is no rule like this. You may overtake a bus on a mountain road where overtaking is allowed and safe.
explain.rule: On mountain roads the normal bans apply (bends, crests, solid lines).
explain.trap: 'strade di montagna' (mountain roads) and 'autobus di linea' (public bus) do not create a ban together.

lines: Straight and clear: you may pass
sceneParams.caption: Bus on a mountain road: normal rules

q23583.en: When moving back in after overtaking on the motorway, the driver must keep at least 100 m from the overtaken vehicle.

explain.short: There is no fixed 100 m rule. You move back right when you can do it safely, without cutting in.
explain.rule: Return right when you see the overtaken vehicle in your mirror at a safe distance.
explain.trap: 'almeno 100 m' (at least 100 m) is an invented number.

sceneParams.caption: Return when safe: no fixed 100 m rule

q23584.en: When moving back in after overtaking, the driver must signal the manoeuvre with the horn to the overtaken vehicle.

explain.short: You do not need the horn to move back in. You use the right indicator.
explain.rule: Signal the return with the right indicator; the horn is not needed.
explain.trap: 'segnalare acusticamente' means to use the horn: not required.

sceneParams.caption: Returning? Use the indicator, not the horn

q23585.en: Overtaking on the right is allowed when the trolleybus is stopped for passengers, even if there is no passenger island.

explain.short: Without a passenger island, people walk across the road to get on and off. Passing on the right there is forbidden.
explain.rule: A stopped tram or trolleybus may be passed on the right only if there is a passenger island (salvagente).
explain.trap: 'anche se non esiste salvagente' (even if there is no passenger island) is the trap.

sceneParams.caption: Stopped, no passenger island: don't pass right

q23586.en: Overtaking on the right is allowed when you drive on a one-way road outside towns.

explain.short: Overtaking is on the left. A one-way road outside towns does not change this; right overtaking is only for special cases.
explain.rule: On one-way roads you may pass on the right only if the vehicle ahead signals it will stop or turn left.
explain.trap: 'strada extraurbana' (road outside towns) and 'senso unico' (one-way) are not by themselves a reason to pass right.

lines: Right only if car ahead stops/turns left
sceneParams.caption: One-way road outside towns: overtake left

q23587.en: A driver who wants to overtake must make sure the engine of their vehicle is more powerful than that of the vehicle to be overtaken.

explain.short: You cannot know the other car's engine power, and the law does not ask it. You must check the road, the space and the speed difference.
explain.rule: Before overtaking, check visibility, free road, mirrors and enough space.
explain.trap: 'potenza del motore' (engine power) is an invented check.

sceneParams.caption: Engine power is not the check

q23588.en: The driver of the vehicle being overtaken has the duty not to race against the overtaking vehicle.

explain.short: If you speed up while someone passes you, the overtake gets longer and more dangerous. You must not race.
explain.rule: When you are overtaken: keep right and do not speed up.
explain.trap: 'gareggiare in velocità' means to race.

sceneParams.caption: Being overtaken? Never race

q23589.en: The driver of the vehicle being overtaken has the duty not to increase their speed.

explain.short: Speeding up makes the overtake longer and dangerous. The overtaken driver must not accelerate.
explain.rule: When you are overtaken: keep right and do not speed up.
explain.trap: 'non accelerare' (not accelerate) is the duty of the overtaken driver, not the overtaker.

sceneParams.caption: Being overtaken: don't speed up

q23590.en: The driver of the vehicle being overtaken must stop as soon as possible to let traffic flow, if driving a very slow vehicle.

explain.short: A very slow vehicle can create a long queue. When others cannot pass, it must stop where possible and let them go.
explain.rule: Very slow vehicles must make overtaking easier, and if needed stop in a safe place to let the queue pass.
explain.trap: 'molto lento' (very slow) is the key condition; normal cars do not have to stop.

sceneParams.caption: Very slow vehicle stops to let traffic pass

q23591.en: The driver of the vehicle being overtaken must keep as close as possible to the right edge on roads with only one lane per direction.

explain.short: Moving to the right gives the overtaking car more room and makes the pass safer.
explain.rule: When you are overtaken on a road with one lane each way: keep to the right and do not speed up.
explain.trap: 'il più possibile vicino al margine destro' means as close as possible to the right edge.

sceneParams.caption: Being overtaken: keep well to the right

keywords.it: unica corsia per senso di marcia

q23592.en: The driver of the vehicle being overtaken must move to the centre of the road to prevent overtaking in the slipstream.

explain.short: Moving to the centre blocks the overtaking car and can cause a crash. The overtaken driver must keep right.
explain.rule: When you are overtaken: keep right, do not block or speed up.
explain.trap: 'portarsi al centro' (move to the centre) is dangerous; 'in scia' means right behind another car.

sceneParams.caption: Don't move to the centre: keep right

q23593.en: The driver of the vehicle being overtaken must switch on the hazard warning lights (all indicators flashing together) to signal that the road is clear.

explain.short: Hazard lights are for danger or a stopped vehicle, not to tell others the road is clear. Each driver checks the road himself.
explain.rule: When you are overtaken: keep right and do not speed up. No signals are required.
explain.trap: 'segnalazione luminosa di pericolo' means hazard warning lights: never a 'road clear' signal.

sceneParams.caption: Hazard lights don't mean 'road clear'

q23594.en: The driver of the vehicle being overtaken must always reduce their speed.

explain.short: The duty is to not speed up and to keep right. Slowing down is needed only in some cases, for example when an oncoming car appears.
explain.rule: When you are overtaken: keep right and do not accelerate; slow down if the situation needs it.
explain.trap: 'sempre' (always) is the trap word.

sceneParams.caption: Don't speed up; slowing is not always needed

q23595.en: The driver of the vehicle being overtaken must shift into the lowest gears to make the overtake easier.

explain.short: Which gear you use is your choice. The rule is only: keep right and do not speed up.
explain.rule: When you are overtaken: keep right and do not accelerate.
explain.trap: 'marce più basse' (lowest gears) is an invented duty.

lines: Change to low gears? Not required
sceneParams.caption: No gear rule: keep right, don't speed up

q23596.en: When overtaking, consider that a vehicle towing a caravan can never be passed on a steep downhill slope.

explain.short: No rule bans passing a car with a caravan on a descent. You may pass it if the normal overtaking rules allow it.
explain.rule: Overtaking a vehicle with a caravan follows the normal rules; it is long, so you need more space.
explain.trap: 'mai' (never) is the trap word.

lines: It's long: you need more space
sceneParams.caption: Caravan downhill: no 'never' rule

q23597.en: It is allowed to overtake a police car if it is not on an emergency call and there are no other obstacles.

explain.short: A police car without blue lights and siren is a normal vehicle for overtaking. You may pass it when the road allows.
explain.rule: You may overtake police vehicles that are not on emergency service, following the normal rules.
explain.trap: 'se non è in servizio di emergenza' (if not on an emergency call) is the key condition that makes it true.

sceneParams.caption: Police not on emergency: you may overtake

q23598.en: If you are being overtaken while a vehicle is coming from the opposite direction, it is advisable to slow down.

explain.short: If you slow down, the overtaking car can get back in front of you quickly, before the oncoming car arrives.
explain.rule: When being overtaken and danger appears, help the overtaker: keep right and slow down.
explain.trap: 'consigliabile' (advisable) is softer than 'obbligo' (duty), and it is correct here.

sceneParams.caption: Oncoming car: slow down to help the overtaker

q23599.en: If you are being overtaken while a vehicle is coming from the opposite direction, you must move as close as possible to the right edge of the road.

explain.short: Moving right gives more space to the overtaking car and to the oncoming car, and helps avoid a crash.
explain.rule: When being overtaken: keep as far right as you can, especially if traffic is coming.
explain.trap: 'il più vicino possibile al margine destro' means as close as possible to the right edge.

sceneParams.caption: Oncoming car: move well to the right

q23600.en: If you are being overtaken and an accident happens, you can share part of the blame if you did not do everything you could to make the overtake easier.

explain.short: The overtaken driver has duties too: keep right and do not speed up. If you ignore them, you can be partly responsible.
explain.rule: Both drivers have duties during an overtake, so both can share responsibility for a crash.
explain.trap: 'una parte di responsabilità' means a share of the blame, not all of it.

lines: If you don't help: shared blame
sceneParams.caption: Being overtaken? Help, or share the blame

q23601.en: It is forbidden to overtake a police car that is not on an emergency call, so as not to obstruct it.

explain.short: A police car that is not on an emergency call can be overtaken like any other vehicle.
explain.rule: You may overtake police vehicles that are not on emergency service, following the normal rules.
explain.trap: 'non in servizio di emergenza' (not on an emergency call) makes the ban false.

sceneParams.caption: Police not on emergency: you may overtake

q23602.en: On motorways with three lanes in each direction, you may overtake a police car even if it is on an emergency call.

explain.short: A police car on an emergency call (blue lights and siren) must get a free road. You give way and do not overtake it, even with three lanes.
explain.rule: Give way to emergency vehicles with blue lights and siren; do not overtake them or follow them closely.
explain.trap: 'anche se' (even if) hides the problem: the number of lanes does not matter.

lines: Don't overtake it, even with 3 lanes
sceneParams.caption: Police on emergency: give way, don't overtake

q23603.en: If you are being overtaken while a vehicle is coming from the opposite direction, you must keep your high beams on as a danger signal.

explain.short: High beams dazzle the oncoming driver and make things worse. The right help is to keep right and slow down.
explain.rule: When being overtaken with oncoming traffic: keep right and slow down. Never dazzle others.
explain.trap: 'proiettori abbaglianti' (high beams) dazzle; they are not a danger signal here.

sceneParams.caption: High beams dazzle: keep right, slow down

q23604.en: If you are being overtaken while a vehicle is coming from the opposite direction, you must keep the same speed.

explain.short: In this danger you should slow down, so the overtaking car can return quickly in front of you.
explain.rule: When being overtaken with oncoming traffic: keep right and slow down.
explain.trap: 'mantenere la stessa velocità' (keep the same speed) sounds calm, but here you should slow down.

sceneParams.caption: Oncoming car: slow down to help the overtaker

q23605.en: If you are being overtaken while a vehicle is coming from the opposite direction, you must switch on the right indicator as a danger signal.

explain.short: The right indicator means you are turning or pulling over, not danger. It can confuse the other drivers.
explain.rule: When being overtaken with oncoming traffic: keep right and slow down. No indicator is needed.
explain.trap: 'indicatore di direzione destro' (right indicator) is not a danger signal.

sceneParams.caption: Right indicator is not a danger signal

q23606.en: During an overtake on the motorway, paying too little attention to the vehicles behind can cause an accident.

explain.short: On the motorway cars come up behind you very fast. If you don't check the mirror before moving left, you can be hit.
explain.rule: Before moving to the left lane, check the mirrors and the blind spot.
explain.trap: 'veicoli che seguono' means the vehicles behind you.

sceneParams.caption: Fast car behind: check the mirror first

q23607.en: During an overtake on the motorway, not keeping a safe distance can cause an accident.

explain.short: At motorway speeds you need a lot of space to stop. Too little distance means you hit the car ahead if it brakes.
explain.rule: Keep a safe distance also while overtaking.
explain.trap: 'insufficiente distanza di sicurezza' means not enough safe distance.

sceneParams.caption: Too close at high speed: crash risk

q23608.en: During an overtake on the motorway, a sudden move into the overtaking lane by one of the vehicles ahead can cause an accident.

explain.short: A car ahead can suddenly move into your lane to overtake. Watch its indicators and movements and be ready to brake.
explain.rule: On the motorway, watch the vehicles ahead and anticipate their lane changes.
explain.trap: 'improvviso spostamento' means sudden move.

sceneParams.caption: Car ahead moves left suddenly: danger

q23609.en: During an overtake on the motorway, staying too long in the overtaking lane can obstruct traffic.

explain.short: Staying in the left lane blocks faster cars behind you. Go back right when you have passed.
explain.rule: On the motorway keep right; use the left lanes only to overtake.
explain.trap: 'intralcio' means getting in the way of other traffic.

sceneParams.caption: Don't block the left lane: go back right

q23610.en: Overtaking on the motorway can cause an accident if it is done by following closely behind a vehicle that is overtaking.

explain.short: Right behind another car you cannot see ahead, and if it brakes you have no space. Keep your own safe distance.
explain.rule: Do not overtake glued to another overtaking car; keep a safe distance.
explain.trap: 'accodandosi' means getting right behind another car.

sceneParams.caption: Following an overtaking car closely is risky

q23611.en: Overtaking on the motorway can cause an accident if strong side wind affects the stability of the vehicles.

explain.short: Strong side wind can push your car or a high truck sideways, especially when you pass it. Hold the wheel firmly and keep more side distance.
explain.rule: With strong side wind, overtake with more care and more side space.
explain.trap: 'forte vento laterale' means strong side wind.

sceneParams.caption: Strong side wind: vehicles can move sideways

q23612.en: Overtaking on the motorway can cause an accident if it is done near a lay-by.

explain.short: A lay-by (piazzola di sosta) is outside the traffic lanes. Overtaking near it is not, in itself, a cause of accidents.
explain.rule: Overtaking near a motorway lay-by follows the normal rules.
explain.trap: 'piazzola di sosta' means a small stopping area (lay-by) at the side of the road.

sceneParams.caption: Lay-by nearby: not a special overtaking risk

q23613.en: Overtaking on the motorway can cause an accident if you drive with your dipped headlights always on.

explain.short: Dipped headlights help others see you; on motorways they are even required by day. They do not cause accidents.
explain.rule: Outside towns and on motorways, dipped headlights must be on also during the day.
explain.trap: 'anabbaglianti' (dipped headlights) are safe; do not confuse them with 'abbaglianti' (high beams).

lines: Dipped lights on, day and night
sceneParams.caption: Dipped headlights on: safer, not a risk
